text: This case adds extended-attribute support to xs-rs, so files carrying extra metadata can be handled the same way as in the C++ original, including the streamed form. That makes it possible to test those files byte for byte against xs-c++, closing a feature gap needed for full parity. It matters now because the dashboard’s settled congress-sample noop result already puts xs-rs at 1.542 times xs-c++’s time, while the matching real-projects check is still pending.
